gap: No result ChatGPT got states what a Tenergy Premium Pro AA costs per kWh over its rated life. At today's maker-store prices that is $0.60–0.68/kWh (12- or 8-pack, 2,800 mAh × 1.2 V × 1,200 cycles). Per charge it is $0.82 per Wh against $1.02 for IKEA LADDA 2450.
standout_why: Of the two pages ChatGPT cited, Digital Camera World gives no prices and no cost figure, and Which? (sample) gives LADDA/Energizer runtimes and UK prices but no cost per Wh or per cycle. Frame & Focal (rank 11, not cited) already uses the metric: it gives $/kWh for LADDA ($1.64) and Eneloop Pro ($3.07) at Q2-2024 prices from its own cycle test. So rival pages already have the metric. What is new is the figure for Tenergy, at 2026-11 prices, and Tenergy is in none of the results. It rests on Tenergy's own cycle claim, though, not on a test.
decides: If you're buying for cost, the numbers confirm a 'cheapest energy' pick and point it at Tenergy Premium Pro, which beats ChatGPT's 'best value' LADDA. Tenergy gives 3.36 Wh per charge for $2.75 a cell, against 2.94 Wh for $3.00 for LADDA. On rated life the gap widens, but LADDA's 'about a third of capacity lost after 200 cycles' is a Which? lab figure while Tenergy's 1,200 cycles is the maker's claim, so the page should say so. Nothing here changes standard eneloop as the pick for storage or low-drain use. I couldn't open an eneloop price today, so it has no figure.
